subject: Unexpected invoiced overage — parallel ingest / attribution question
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightwire.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightWire Finance <invoices@brightwire.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected invoiced overage — parallel ingest / attribution question

Hi Monica,

We received June invoices this morning and there is a ~28% overage compared to our forecast tied to an "embed ingestion" line item (line 4). Our engineering team pulled a short-term parallel ingest to speed a migration on 2026-06-09, but we accounted for that internally and expected the usage to attribute to the staging API key. The invoice shows the tokens billed to our production tenant. Can you confirm whether our parallel ingest could have been double-attributed or mis-tagged?

I've attached a small CSV with our internal job IDs and timestamps (brightwire_usage_snapshot.csv). We need a breakdown because finance can't clear payment until we reconcile.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Finance Operations — BrightWire
[invoices@brightwire.ai]

[Attachment: brightwire_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightwire.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected invoiced overage — parallel ingest / attribution question

Samantha — thanks for the note and the CSV. I'm sorry for the surprise here. We will investigate attribution immediately.

Quick plan:
- Ben from Billing will pull the raw per-request attribution for 2026-06-08 -> 2026-06-10.
- I'll ask Engineering (David) to look at whether a parallel ingest could have generated duplicate session IDs or re-used the production API key.
- We'll share a concise evidence pack (request IDs, timestamps, model, and token counts) within 48 hours.

In the meantime, if BrightWire wants to withhold payment pending reconciliation, we can place the invoice on hold and mark it as "under review" in our billing portal. Let me know which PO/reference you want us to tie to the hold.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0194

[Attachment: redwood_acknowledgement_note.txt (text, 1KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightWire overage — raw logs request

Forwarding BrightWire's CSV and Monica's ack. I'm pulling the per-request attribution export now; export job will include request_id, api_key_label, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, timestamp. ETA ~2 hours.

Note to David: please prioritize checking for:
- multiple request records with identical request_id or client_side_session_id across both staging and production keys,
- cases where an SDK retry generated new request_ids but re-used the same KV or session,
- unusually high batching events on 2026-06-09 between 02:00-04:00 UTC.

Forwarded attachments: brightwire_usage_snapshot.csv

—Ben
Billing & Revenue Operations, Redwood

[Attachment: brightwire_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightWire overage — raw logs request

Quick summary of findings (initial pass):
- We found ~9,200 requests from BrightWire between 2026-06-09T02:15:03Z and 2026-06-09T03:48:49Z that were attributed to the production tenant (prod-key-XXXX).
- The same job IDs appear in BrightWire's CSV, but ~7,100 of those requests also have a duplicate entry where the request payload included a client-side retry header (x-client-retry-id), which our attribution pipeline incorrectly treated as separate sessions rather than deduplicating on retry id.
- Root cause: our request de-duplication heuristic skipped dedupe when a batching-level checksum was present (introduced in an SDK patch on 2026-05-31) and some parallel ingest clients set both a batching checksum and client-side retry id. Our pipeline now discards the batching checksum for dedupe decisions.

Impact estimate: ~18% of the billed tokens in that window are duplicates attributable to retries during parallel ingest. I have exported the session log subset and attached it (redwood_session_logs_20260611.zip).

Next steps:
1) Billing needs to compute token-level credit for the duplicated request_ids.
2) Monica/Ben: offer BrightWire a reconciliation report and propose a credit.
3) Engineering: we will ship a backfill that tags the duplicate requests and export a corrected usage CSV for the billing system. ETA for corrected CSV: EOD Monday 2026-06-15.

—David Kim
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_session_logs_20260611.zip (ZIP, 2.8MB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightwire.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, BrightWire Finance <invoices@brightwire.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected invoiced overage — parallel ingest / attribution question

Samantha — thanks for your patience. We've completed the investigation and attached the corrected usage CSV and evidence pack. Summary:

- Cause: a mix of client-side retries + our SDK batching checksum behavior caused duplicate attribution for a subset of requests on 2026-06-09.
- Scope: approximately 18% of the tokens billed in the disputed window were duplicate counts.
- Action taken: billing has produced a corrected usage export and applied a credit of USD 16,920 (pro-rated to the duplicate tokens). The credit appears as line item CR-20260615 on your invoice.
- Invoice status: We've placed the June invoice on hold per your request, marked with PO 12345. Once you confirm the PO and accept the credit, we will clear the hold and resume normal payment terms.

If you want, we can also schedule a brief 30-minute postmortem walkthrough with Engineering (David) and Billing (Ben) to go over the logs and the fix strategy.

Next steps for BrightWire:
1) Reply to this thread confirming PO 12345 for the hold, or provide alternate reference.
2) If you accept the credit, we'll mark the invoice as reconciled and share an updated statement.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we'll continue monitoring for SDK-related dedupe issues and will alert customers proactively if we see similar signs.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0194

[Attachments: corrected_usage_20260611.csv (CSV, 18KB), evidence_pack_BW-2026-06-11.pdf (PDF, 420KB), PO_12345.pdf (PDF, 32KB)]
